target_customer: Consumers who record and share video on iPhones
problem: Phone video was shaky and hard to edit; users wanted stabilization, filters and zoom that could be changed after recording.
business_model: Free consumer app, no revenue model reported
product_category: Consumer video capture and sharing app

founders.name: Alex Karpenko
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Alex Karpenko and Alexei Karpenko as two separate entries, possibly the same person, so one founder is recorded. TechCrunch 2013 says Luma was previously in Stanford StartX.

exit.reason: Instagram bought the team and technology; the app was pulled from the App Store and supported until Dec 31, 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time video stabilization and rolling shutter correction on 2012 phone hardware were hard engineering problems for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: The stabilization technology was valuable enough that Instagram bought it, but the sharing network around it had no lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Instagram added video in June 2013 and bought Luma in August 2013, its first acquisition, using the technology for video stabilization.

market_need_then: Phone video quality and sharing were growing; Instagram video and Vine launched in 2013, showing demand for mobile video sharing.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found no source on the rename or identity; press about it was the Instagram acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Midnox, renamed Luma, built real time video stabilization and filters in a consumer app and sold the team and technology to Instagram in August 2013. The app was shut down, so the outcome was a technology acquihire driven by the engineering rather than by user traction, with no disclosed price.
notes: midnox.com failed DNS resolution (dead or blocked). Funding not found; a CB Insights page for 'Luma' with Venrock may be a different company and is not used. No dated competitor sources near the January 2012 batch were found. Founding year unknown.
